causes.description: Lending to, or funds placed with, parties connected to the institution or its owners.
Misrepresented or misreported its true financial position to the Bank of Ghana.
A large share of the loan book not being repaid.
Weak corporate governance, such as the absence of a functioning board.
Changed its name, head office, branches or structure without the Bank of Ghana's prior approval.
Did not implement the Bank of Ghana's on-site examination recommendations.
Did not publish its audited financial statements as the law requires.
Stopped submitting prudential returns to the Bank of Ghana.
Ceased operations and closed its offices to the general public.

institutions.institution_name: Alpha Capital Savings and Loans Ltd.

institutions.notes: Net worth POSITIVE at GHS 628,311.16 - the only institution of the 23 not reporting a deficit. Still revoked: CAR -81.39%, insolvent since Oct 2016, no functioning board.
Took over Ivory Finance Company (operating since 2000). Exposure to affiliates at 319% against a 25% regulatory limit.
Formerly Sterling Savings and Loans, part of Nordcom Africa Holdings. Distinct from Sterling Financial Services Ltd. (entry 21).
Originally Apex Finance House (1997). Entire loan portfolio non-performing.
Changed name to El Finance Limited and relocated head office without BoG approval. Over-exposed to six related companies.

institutions.institution_name: Express Savings and Loans Company Ltd.
institutions.notes: Closed 14 of its 18 branches by May 2019 without BoG approval. Cash reserve ratio 0.23% against a 10% minimum.

institutions.institution_name: First African Savings & Loans Company Ltd.
First Allied Savings and Loans Co. Ltd.
institutions.notes: Largest net-worth deficit of the 23. NPLs at 88.89% of the loan portfolio. Deposit liabilities understated to conceal losses. Bank run began June 2018 at the Kumasi and Adabraka branches and spread to all 27.

institutions.institution_name: First Ghana Savings and Loans Co. Ltd.
institutions.notes: Established 1956 as First Ghana Building Society under the Building Societies Ordinance 1955 - the oldest institution in the dataset, predating independence. Notably few stated causes: no related-party lending, no misreporting, no fraud. A straightforward capital failure.
Formerly EZI Savings and Loans (licensed 2007), acquired by Ideal Financial Holdings 2014. Cash reserve ratio 0.07% against a 10% minimum.

institutions.institution_name: Global Access Savings and Loans Company Ltd.
institutions.notes: Began as a Western Union agent for ADB. Assumed a GHS 2.91m loan of the majority shareholder, injected it as equity, and concealed the liability in a suspense account.

Formerly First National Savings and Loans; universal banking licence Sep 2014 as GN Bank; reclassified to savings and loans 4 Jan 2019 after failing the GHS 400m minimum capital. GHS 761.55m placed with sister companies (Groupe Nduom). USD 62.26m, GBP 718,528 and EUR 4,200 of depositor funds transferred to a US affiliate without documentation.

annotation.text: In May 2026 the Court of Appeal ordered the Bank of Ghana to restore this licence. The Supreme Court stayed that judgment in July 2026, pending the appeal, so the licence has not been restored. The figures and causes here are as the Bank of Ghana stated them in 2019, and this project takes no position on the litigation.

institutions.notes: Figures are as at end-November 2018, not May 2019 - the institution stopped submitting returns after that date. Proposed merger with FirsTrust declined by BoG: both insolvent, merged entity assessed at CAR -78.32%.

institutions.institution_name: Legacy Capital Savings and Loans Ltd.
institutions.notes: Operated as a microfinance institution from Oct 2013 before its savings and loans licence in Aug 2016.

institutions.institution_name: Midland Savings and Loans Company Ltd.
institutions.notes: Related-party exposure to Liberty Asset Management, Liberty DMI Microfinance and Griffin Financial Services.
CAR is as at end-MARCH 2010, not 2019. Stopped submitting returns May 2010 and folded operations in 2011 without notifying BoG. Licence not revoked until Aug 2019 - a nine-year gap.
Formerly Kantamanto Savings and Loans; acquired by Hoda Group 2006. Non-performing exposure of GHS 160.10m to sister company uniSecurities.
